question: How can a deaf student follow a lecture?
slides: *22%* of deaf US adults hold a bachelor's.
description: A deaf student can follow a lecture with a booked CART captioner or an interpreter, and the live captions app Captio AI is one more tool.
Captio AI is made for deaf and hard of hearing people and shows a lecturer's words on your phone during an in-person lecture.
According to the National Deaf Center, 22% of deaf people in the US aged 25 to 64 had a bachelor's degree or higher in 2022, 15.7 points below hearing peers.
A deaf student can read live captions in a lecture instead of lip-reading.
Captio AI on iPhone keeps recording and captioning a lecture with the screen locked, and the Lock Screen shows a timer, so unlock to read the words.
A student can add course terms and names to Words and names in Captio AI before a lecture starts.
Ask the lecturer before you record a lecture.
Captio AI turns a saved lecture into key points, detailed notes or questions and answers.
Captio AI captions can contain mistakes and do not replace a captioner, an interpreter or a college's accommodations.
